To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the protein(s) responsible for the "LHRH-statin" activity in RTF has a molecular mass of 30-35 kD, that it has a molecular mass similar to that of inhibin, and that it is not inhibin 32k.
the rete testes fluid protein that suppresses LHRH pulses is not inhibin.
the rete testicular fluid of sheep contains a factor able to suppress LH secretion in a central manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms of the central control of gonadotropins in the sheep.
the characterization of a protein(s) present within RTF that can inhibit the release of LH.
the identification and characterization of a new protein(s) in RTF that is able to inhibit LH secretion in sheep.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the "LHRH-statin" activity of RTF is not mediated by inhibin 32 K, but rather by other protein(s) present within this fluid.
inhibin 31K is not the factor present in RTF that suppresses LH pulses.
the "LHRH-statin" protein present in RTF is neither inhibin 32k nor any other protein present in bovine follicular fluids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the "LHRH stator" is a protein present in RTF and that inhibin is not this protein.
inhibin is not involved in the central effect of RTF on LH secretion.

the "LHRH stainer" is not a gonadal protein, is present in ovine rete testis but not in bovine rete testis, is a peptide of molecular weight lower than 20 kDa, and is present in the ovine rete fluid in an inactive form.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the "LHRH stantin" is not inhibin 32k.
inhibin is not a factor responsible for the "LHRH-statin" activity of RTF.
inhibin 31K is not the factor responsible for LHRH inhibition in sheep.
